# NEAR is a three-layer business

> **NEAR isn't just an L1 anymore. It's a three-layer business, and the token is only beginning to capture that value.**

Investment thesis, NEAR HACKATHON (Investment Thesis track). Data as of Nov 6, 2026. Every number in this document is computed from files in `data/` by `make charts`, which also rebuilds the charts and the dashboard (`site/index.html`, where each chart shows the query behind it). This is research, not investment advice.

## Summary

NEAR is still discussed as a smart-contract L1, and on L1 metrics alone it looks like a network in decline: L1 transactions fell from 7.2M a day in Jan 2025 to 729.9K in Oct 2026. That view misses where the business went. NEAR now has three layers, and most of the money comes from the second.

| Layer | What it is | Latest |
|---|---|---|
| **NEAR L1** | The base chain: accounts, contracts, gas | 729.9K transactions a day; 8.9% of them go to Intents |
| **NEAR Intents** | Swaps between assets on any chains, settled on NEAR | $10.4B of volume and $14.9M of fees in 2026 Q3; 58% of native cross-chain swap volume |
| **NEAR AI** | NEAR AI Cloud: private, verifiable inference on open models, paid per token or by staking NEAR | 299.8B tokens a week on OpenRouter; 1.4M NEAR staked for inference |

**Key takeaways**

- Intents earned 95% of NEAR's protocol revenue over Aug 2026–Oct 2026, up from 34% a year earlier.
- Intents handled 58% of native cross-chain swap volume in Oct 2026, up from 45% a year earlier.
- NEAR AI served 299.8B tokens a week on OpenRouter by Nov 1, 2026, 21× its first full week, and 1.4M NEAR is staked for NEAR AI.
- In 2026 Q3, burns and Intents revenue offset 19.5% of new NEAR, up from 1.8% a year earlier. In the base scenario with HSP-029, new supply is fully offset by Jan 2029.

### Follow the money

![Follow the money: where NEAR's value came from in 2026 Q3](site/charts/money-flow.svg)

In 2026 Q3, users paid $14.9M in Intents fees on $10.4B of swaps (0.14%). NEAR kept $3.7M (25%; the rest went to partner apps and solvers), worth 1.5M NEAR, which funds buybacks: the buyback wallet grew by 1.4M NEAR over the quarter. With 66.4K NEAR burned by L1 gas fees, 1.6M NEAR was captured, 19.5% of the 8.2M NEAR issued in the quarter.

---

## Part 1. Isn't just an L1 anymore

### C1. Most of NEAR's revenue now comes from beyond the L1

**Evidence.** NEAR's share of Intents fees overtook the L1 fee burn in Oct 2025. Over the last three months (Aug 2026–Oct 2026), Intents was 95.1% of the value the protocol kept (97.8% of all fees paid). Since Jan 2026, Intents has been above 82% of protocol revenue every month.

![NEAR protocol revenue by source, monthly](site/charts/c1-revenue.svg)

![Intents share of NEAR's protocol revenue, monthly](site/charts/c1-share.svg)

**Counterpoint.** Part of the shift is the L1 shrinking rather than Intents growing. L1 fees burned fell from $567K in Jan 2025 to $25K–$47K a month in Apr 2026–Aug 2026, as the largest L1 app left (C2) and the NEAR price fell from about $5.12 to $1.80. L1 gas is also cheap by design, so L1 revenue was never large.

### C2. The L1 is becoming Intents' settlement layer

**Evidence.** L1 transactions fell from 7.2M a day in Jan 2025 to 729.9K in Oct 2026, mostly as KaiChing and HOT wound down. Transactions to intents.near rose from 28.4K to 65K a day over Jan 2026–Oct 2026. Intents' share of L1 transactions rose from 0.8% in Jan 2026 to 8.9% in Oct 2026. Leaving out KaiChing and HOT, it went from 4.7% to 10.6%.

![NEAR L1 transactions per day, by app](site/charts/c2-l1-tx.svg)

![Intents share of NEAR L1 transactions, monthly](site/charts/c2-share.svg)

**Counterpoint.** Most of the rising share is the rest of the L1 shrinking. KaiChing accounts sent 65% of all L1 transactions in March 2026; when they stopped, they caused 87% of April's fall. Transactions to intents.near were higher in Jul 2025 (109.8K a day) than in Oct 2026 (65K), though Intents volume is 17× larger now, so transaction counts don't track Intents' growth. Without KaiChing and HOT, the share was 14.9% in Jul 2025, above today's 10.6%.

## Part 2. A three-layer business

### C3. Intents is a real, broad-based growth engine

Covers the 1Click channel only, about 27% of Intents volume in Oct 2026. The first 1Click swap in the data is on Mar 27, 2025.

**Evidence.** In Oct 2026, 1Click handled 505.9K swaps worth $1.1B from 269K distinct users, through 352 referrer apps and 785 chain pairs. A year earlier (Oct 2025): 132.6K users, 48 apps and 338 chain pairs. 91% of Oct 2026 volume moved between two chains other than NEAR. Swaps started on 37 chains; the largest was Ethereum at 31%.

![NEAR Intents 1Click swap volume per day](site/charts/c3-volume.svg)

![Distinct 1Click users per month](site/charts/c3-users.svg)

![Where 1Click swaps start, by origin chain](site/charts/c3-chains.svg)

**Counterpoint.** Activity is concentrated in trading flows and a few apps. In Oct 2026, 34% of 1Click volume was stablecoin-to-stablecoin (up from 9% a year earlier) and 74% involved a stablecoin. One referrer app (swapkit) routed 40% of volume, and the top 10 users 15% (up from 11% a year earlier). Zcash was 14% of origin volume. Confidential trades are masked in the Explorer data.

### C4. Intents is gaining share, not just moving with the market

**Evidence.** Among native cross-chain swap venues tracked by DefiLlama, Intents' share of volume rose from 45% in Oct 2025 to 58% in Oct 2026, after peaking at 79% in Jun 2026. Over the 12 months to Oct 2026, Intents volume rose 131% while total DEX volume fell 56% and bridge-aggregator volume rose 118%.

![NEAR Intents share of native cross-chain swap volume, monthly](site/charts/c4-share.svg)

![Monthly volume, indexed](site/charts/c4-index.svg)

**Counterpoint.** The share has eased since its Jun 2026 peak (79% → 58%). The peer set misses large bridges whose data is paid (Relay, deBridge, Across, Mayan), which overstates the level. Bridge aggregators grew 118% over the same 12 months, close to Intents' 131%. Recent swings move with the market: in Sep 2026 Intents volume rose 73% while bridge aggregators rose 92% and all DEX volume rose 30%; in Oct 2026 the three moved -17%, -11% and -17%.

### C5. NEAR AI is a working third layer

NEAR AI Cloud sells private, verifiable inference. Open models run inside trusted execution environments (TEEs), so neither NEAR AI nor the hardware operator can read prompts, and each response can be checked against a hardware attestation. Customers pay per token through an OpenAI-compatible API, or stake NEAR and receive inference credits paid from the staking rewards.

**Evidence.**
- **Usage.** NEAR AI served 299.8B tokens through OpenRouter in the week to Nov 1, 2026, up from 14.4B in its first full week (to Sep 20, 2026). At list prices that week was worth about $26K, or $1.4M a year.
- **Staking.** NEAR staked with NEAR AI's validator rose from 10K on Jul 10, 2026 to 1.4M on Nov 5, 2026. 119 accounts stake for NEAR AI Cloud credits, and 84 have subscribed to NEAR AI Agents.
- **Product.** 64 models in the NEAR AI Cloud catalog, 18 of them running in TEEs for verifiable private inference.
- **Distribution.** Since Oct 15, 2026, Brave's AI assistant Leo runs GLM 5.3 Flash on NEAR AI Cloud in the production browser. Brave has over 128M monthly users, though only Leo users who pick that model use NEAR AI Cloud. NEAR AI also names Venice, the Government of Bermuda and Abound as customers.
- **Developers.** IronClaw, NEAR AI's open-source agent OS, has 12.7K GitHub stars.

![Tokens NEAR AI serves on OpenRouter, per week](site/charts/c5-tokens.svg)

![NEAR staked with NEAR AI's validator](site/charts/c5-stake.svg)

**Counterpoint.** NEAR AI doesn't publish revenue; our OpenRouter estimate is about $1.4M a year, and OpenRouter is one channel among several. Staking is concentrated: the largest staker holds 73% of the credits farm and the top 10 hold 96%. Staking funds about $13.7K of credits a month, and contract activity has been flat at 168–391 calls a week.

## Part 3. The token is only beginning to capture that value

### When the mechanisms switched on

NEAR's issuance fell from 5.0% to 2.5% a year at the Oct 2025 cut. Every mechanism that sends value to the token has switched on since: buybacks on Feb 23, 2026, staking for NEAR AI on Jul 30, 2026 and burning all L1 gas on Nov 5, 2026. HSP-029 (passed Nov 2, 2026) would lower issuance to 1.6% by Jan 2029.

![When each value-capture mechanism switched on](site/charts/timeline.svg)

| Mechanism | Since | What it does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Issuance cap cut from 5% to 2.5% | Oct 30, 2025 | Halves the NEAR issued each year | Protocol config via archival RPC; visible in BigQuery supply flows |
| All L1 gas burned (HSP-027; the 30% rebate to called contracts ends) | Nov 5, 2026 | Every unit of gas paid is destroyed | Protocol config via archival RPC; [vote coverage](https://cryptobriefing.com/near-protocol-governance-eliminates-developer-gas-rebate/) |
| Intents revenue buys back NEAR | Feb 23, 2026 | NEAR's share of Intents fees buys NEAR on the market; it is held in `buybacks.multisignature.near` | [DefiLlama methodology](https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/blob/master/fees/near-intents) |
| Staking for NEAR AI | Jul 30, 2026 | Holders lock NEAR with NEAR AI's validator and receive inference credits | BigQuery (`stake.dao` activity) |
| HSP-029: issuance cap 2.5% → 1.6% | passed Nov 2, 2026; phase-in assumed from Feb 2027 | Lowers the cap evenly over 24 months; not yet in force | [vote coverage](https://cryptobriefing.com/near-protocol-cuts-max-issuance-1-6-percent/) |

### C6. The share of value reaching the token is rising

The capture ratio is the share of newly issued NEAR that is offset in the same period: (NEAR burned by L1 gas + NEAR captured as Intents revenue) ÷ NEAR issued. NEAR newly staked for NEAR AI is shown as a separate line, because it is locked rather than removed.

**Evidence.** NEAR issued per month fell from about 5.3M to 2.7M after the cut, while NEAR captured by the L1 burn and Intents revenue rose to 538.4K in Oct 2026. New stake for NEAR AI added another 664.8K in Aug 2026 and 687.3K in Oct 2026. The capture ratio rose from about 2% a quarter in 2025 Q1–Q3 to 19.5% in 2026 Q3. Counting new AI stake, Aug 2026 reaches 43% and Oct 2026 reaches 44%. 4.1M of the 4.9M NEAR captured as Intents revenue is still in NEAR's three revenue wallets at the end of Oct 2026 (2.1M in the buyback wallet). Bought-back NEAR is held, not burned.

![NEAR issued vs NEAR captured, monthly](site/charts/c6-flows.svg)

![Capture ratio, monthly](site/charts/c6-ratio.svg)

![Revenue-wallet balances, month end](site/charts/c6-wallets.svg)

**Counterpoint.** The ratio is still small: in 2026 Q3, 81% of new NEAR was not offset. At 2025 Q3's issuance, 2026 Q3's captured NEAR would have offset only 10.0%, so about 53% of the rise comes from the inflation cut rather than more revenue. The L1 burn is now 0.8% of issuance. Bought-back NEAR is held, not burned, and these mechanisms are governance decisions that can change. NEAR staked for NEAR AI is locked, not removed, and can be withdrawn.

### Scenarios

Intents revenue in NEAR grew 115% a year over 2026 Q1 → 2026 Q3. If that growth halves every 2 years (base case), burns and revenue fully offset new supply by Jan 2029 with HSP-029, or Apr 2030 if issuance stays at 2.5%. If it holds (bull), by Aug 2028; with no growth (bear), not within 6 years.

![Scenarios: capture ratio, projected monthly](site/charts/scenarios.svg)

| Issuance path | Scenario | Revenue growth a year at start (NEAR terms) | Growth then | After 1 year | After 3 years | Supply after 6 years | Breakeven | Revenue at breakeven vs today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| With HSP-029 (2.5% → 1.6%) | bear | 0% | – | 22.0% | 29.2% | 1.457B | not within 6 years | – |
| With HSP-029 (2.5% → 1.6%) | base | 115% | halves every 2 years | 40.2% | 135% | 1.457B | Jan 2029 | 3.7× |
| With HSP-029 (2.5% → 1.6%) | bull | 115% | held | 42.9% | 256% | 1.457B | Aug 2028 | 4.1× |
| If HSP-029 isn't implemented (stays 2.5%) | bear | 0% | – | 19.3% | 18.4% | 1.520B | not within 6 years | – |
| If HSP-029 isn't implemented (stays 2.5%) | base | 115% | halves every 2 years | 35.4% | 85.1% | 1.520B | Apr 2030 | 5.9× |
| If HSP-029 isn't implemented (stays 2.5%) | bull | 115% | held | 37.8% | 162% | 1.520B | Feb 2029 | 5.9× |

Projections, not findings. Starting point: 2026 Q3's Intents revenue and L1 burn (a capture ratio of 19.4% in Oct 2026). Growth is in NEAR terms, so a rising NEAR price slows it. L1 burn is held at 2026 Q3's level, scaled to 100% burned from Nov 5, 2026. Lines leave the chart above 200%.

**How much depends on the growth window.** Measured over different recent windows, Intents' revenue growth ranges from 115% to 248% a year. With HSP-029, that puts breakeven between Jan 2028 and Jan 2029, depending on the window and on whether growth holds or fades. The scenarios use 2026 Q1 → 2026 Q3 (115% a year).

| Trailing window | Growth a year (NEAR terms) | With HSP-029, growth fades | With HSP-029, growth holds | At 2.5%, growth fades | At 2.5%, growth holds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 Q2 → 2026 Q3 | 181% | Jun 2028 | Mar 2028 | Nov 2028 | Jun 2028 |
| 2026 Q1 → 2026 Q3 | 115% | Jan 2029 | Aug 2028 | Apr 2030 | Feb 2029 |
| 2025 Q4 → 2026 Q3 | 248% | Mar 2028 | Jan 2028 | Jun 2028 | Mar 2028 |

## Part 4. Verdict and what we're watching

### Verdict

**Long-term bullish.** The data supports the first half of the thesis outright. NEAR's revenue no longer depends on the L1: Intents produced 95% of it over Aug 2026–Oct 2026, against 34% a year earlier. Intents isn't just riding the market either. It handled 58% of native cross-chain swap volume in Oct 2026, and its volume grew 131% over the year while total DEX volume fell 56%. NEAR AI is the smallest and newest layer, but it is real: 299.8B tokens a week of paid inference, a production integration in Brave, and 1.4M NEAR staked for credits since staking opened on Jul 30, 2026.

The second half of the thesis, value reaching the token, is a trajectory rather than a fact. Burns and Intents revenue offset 19.5% of new NEAR in 2026 Q3, up from 1.8% a year earlier, but about 53% of that rise came from cutting issuance rather than from more revenue. Most new NEAR is still not offset, and the NEAR bought back is held, not burned.

We lean bullish because of timing. Every mechanism in Part 3 switched on within the last 12 months. The full gas burn has only been live since Nov 5, 2026, HSP-029's cut to 1.6% is not yet in force, and the revenue these mechanisms act on is still growing. In the base scenario, Intents revenue starts at its recent growth rate (115% a year in NEAR terms) and that growth halves every 2 years; with HSP-029, burns and revenue then fully offset new supply by Jan 2029. If the recent rate holds, that comes by Aug 2028; with no growth, it never does. The counterpoints we weigh most are concentration (one referrer app routed 40% of 1Click volume, and one staker holds 73% of the AI credits farm) and governance, since a vote can change any of these mechanisms. Those, and the signposts below, are what would change our view.

### What we're watching

These are the results that would change our mind. Each row gives the latest value, a comparison point and the condition under which we would turn cautious.

| Signpost | Claim | Latest | Earlier | Direction | We'd turn cautious if… |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intents share of NEAR revenue (last 3 months) | C1 | 95.1% | 34.3% a year earlier | ↑ rising | it falls back below half |
| Intents share of L1 transactions | C2 | 8.9% (Oct 2026) | 1.6% a year earlier | ↑ rising | it stops rising over 12 months |
| Intents volume, monthly | C3 | $3.99B (Oct 2026) | $1.72B a year earlier | ↑ rising | growth stalls |
| 1Click distinct users, monthly | C3 | 269K (Oct 2026) | 132.6K a year earlier | ↑ rising | growth stalls |
| Top 10 users' share of 1Click volume | C3 | 15.1% | 21.1% a month earlier | ↓ falling | it rises above half |
| Intents share of native cross-chain volume | C4 | 58.3% (Oct 2026) | 44.5% a year earlier | ↑ rising | it falls over 12 months |
| NEAR AI tokens a week on OpenRouter | C5 | 299.8B (week to Nov 1, 2026) | 50.5B four weeks earlier | ↑ rising | weekly tokens fall for a sustained period |
| NEAR staked for NEAR AI | C5 | 1.4M NEAR (Nov 5, 2026) | 39.3K NEAR on Aug 1, 2026 | ↑ rising | AI staking shrinks |
| Capture ratio, quarterly | C6 | 19.5% (2026 Q3) | 1.8% in 2025 Q3 | ↑ rising | it stops rising after the fee switch |

**Key risks**

- **Competition.** Cross-chain swaps have many venues (bridges, aggregators, THORChain, Chainflip) and wallets can switch routes cheaply, so Intents' share can fall as fast as it rose.
- **Governance.** Buybacks, the fee split and HSP-029 are governance decisions. They can be changed or reversed, and HSP-029 still needs a protocol upgrade.
- **AI execution.** NEAR AI doesn't publish revenue. Its measurable usage sits in a few models on one channel, and AI staking sits with a few accounts.
- **Regulation.** Much of Intents' flow is stablecoins and privacy coins. Rules on cross-chain swaps, front-end apps or privacy assets could restrict it.

## Appendix

### A. Methods

- **Revenue (C1).** L1 side: NEAR burned by gas, measured from block-to-block changes in total supply (BigQuery), valued at the daily NEAR price (NearBlocks). Intents side: NEAR's net revenue after partner payouts, from revenue.near.org. The net basis compares what the protocol keeps on each side; the gross basis compares all fees users pay. L1 gross fees = burn ÷ 0.7 before Nov 5, 2026, while 30% of gas went to the called contract, and = burn from that day, when all gas is burned. Before the switch this is an upper bound, because some gas was always burned in full, so C1's Intents share is conservative.
- **L1 activity (C2).** BigQuery `transactions` table, daily since Jan 2025: transactions, distinct signers (daily active accounts), transactions sent to `intents.near`, the busiest receiving contracts each month, and the two largest consumer apps split out by signer account (KaiChing: `*.kaiching`; HOT: `*.tg` and `hot.tg`). Every query on a block-level table filters on `block_date`; the two balance queries filter on `epoch_date`, the partition column of `ft_balances_daily`.
- **Intents breadth (C3).** NEAR Intents Explorer API, successful swaps. A user is the first sender address of a swap, or its refund address when no sender is given. The top-ten share is the share of a month's volume sent by its ten largest users. Stablecoin shares use the token on each side of the swap.
- **Market share (C4).** DefiLlama daily volumes. Peer set: NEAR Intents, THORChain, Chainflip and Maya Protocol, the venues that swap native assets across chains. Bridge aggregators and total DEX volume are reference series, kept out of the denominator to avoid double counting.
- **NEAR AI (C5).** Tokens per model per day from OpenRouter's NEAR AI provider page. Revenue estimate: NEAR AI's OpenRouter prices for each model, applied with that model's prompt/completion split. Staking from `stake.dao` contract views and archival RPC balances of `nearai.pool.near`; the model catalog from NEAR AI Cloud's public model list.
- **Capture ratio (C6).** Total supply jumps at each epoch boundary by the newly minted NEAR and otherwise only falls, by the NEAR burned; summing those changes gives NEAR issued and burned per day. NEAR captured as Intents revenue comes from revenue.near.org. New AI stake is the month-end change in `nearai.pool.near` stake.
- **Protocol parameters.** Issuance cap and the gas rebate to contracts are read from NEAR's protocol config at past blocks through the archival RPC (`fetch/protocol_history.py`), which dates each change to the day.
- **Scenarios.** The capture ratio is projected monthly from the last complete quarter. NEAR issued is supply × issuance rate ÷ twelve, under HSP-029's phase-in (the main path) and under today's rate. Intents revenue in NEAR starts at its trailing growth rate, measured from the data over the window set in `config.yaml`; the base case lets that growth halve every few years, the bull case holds it, the bear case has none. L1 burn is held at the last quarter's level and scaled up from the day all gas is burned. Inputs are in `config.yaml`.
- **Cross-checks** (`data/derived/crosschecks_monthly.csv`). NEAR price: within 0.5% of CoinGecko in every month. NEAR issued: median gap of 0.5% to the protocol rule (issuance rate × supply). Intents revenue: DefiLlama records NEAR when it is swept into the revenue wallets, in batches, so single months differ; over the last six months the median gap is +25%. L1 gross fees, ours vs DefiLlama +18% and NearBlocks +18% (median monthly gap).

### B. What we couldn't compute

- **NEAR AI Cloud's revenue and total usage.** Its usage and billing APIs need an organisation key, and NEAR AI publishes neither figure. We see OpenRouter traffic and on-chain staking only, and the OpenRouter revenue figure is an estimate at list prices.
- **Intents users and concentration across all channels.** The Explorer API covers the 1Click channel, about 27% of Intents volume in Oct 2026. Swaps through other channels are in the volume figures (revenue.near.org, DefiLlama) but not in the user counts.
- **Confidential swaps.** The Explorer masks them, so they are missing from the user, referrer and chain breakdowns.
- **The whole cross-chain market.** DefiLlama's per-bridge volumes (Relay, deBridge, Across, Mayan and others) are paid-only, so C4's denominator is a peer set, not the whole market.
- **Gas paid by Intents transactions.** We count transactions to `intents.near`. Attributing gas needs receipt-level tables too large for our query budget.
- **Where all captured NEAR went.** 758.1K NEAR captured as Intents revenue is not in the three revenue wallets we track, and we couldn't trace it.
- **Whether AI credits get used.** Credit consumption happens off-chain.
- **A price target.** We don't model one. The thesis is about where value is created and how much of it reaches the token, and there is no reliable multiple for a token whose revenue mostly funds buybacks.

### D. Reproduce

1. `make setup` creates `.venv` and installs the pinned dependencies.
2. `make charts` rebuilds `data/derived/`, every chart, the dashboard and this document from the committed data in a few seconds, with no keys.
3. Open `site/index.html` in a browser: each chart has a hover readout, a table view, its source with date and the query or code behind it.
4. `make verify` picks random past days, months and blocks from the committed data, fetches the same points from each live source and prints both values side by side, in about a minute with no keys. BigQuery's supply figures are checked against the archival RPC. Recent monthly Intents revenue on revenue.near.org is still settling for about three months after each month ends, so a change there is shown as "revised" rather than as a failure. The Explorer check needs the partner key and is skipped without it.

Refreshing the data is optional: `make fetch` (quick sources, no keys), `make fetch-bigquery` (needs a Google Cloud project), `make fetch-explorer` (needs a NEAR Intents partner JWT; slow because of the API's rate limit), `python -m fetch.protocol_history` (slow: the public archival node is rate-limited).

### E. Tools used

Python with requests, pandas, pyarrow, PyYAML and google-cloud-bigquery (pinned in `requirements.txt`). Charts are plain SVG drawn by `viz/svg.py`, with no plotting library; the dashboard's hover layer is `site/app.js`. Code and drafts were written with Claude Code (AI) and reviewed by the author. NEAR agent skills from `near/agent-skills`.
